claims.text: The proposed model integrates DFT-derived anisotropic elastic constants into an extended Callaway formalism.
The model can independently predict lattice and electronic thermal conductivity in HfNbTaTiZr.
Predicted lattice thermal conductivity will be within ±5% of experimental values.
The model will reduce lattice-conductivity prediction error by 20–30% relative to traditional Debye-based estimates.
The model will reduce total-conductivity prediction error by at least 10–15% relative to earlier models that conflate transport channels.
The target HfNbTaTiZr specimen is produced by spark plasma sintering.
The SPS feedstock is gas-atomized HfNbTaTiZr powder.
The processed HfNbTaTiZr is a single-phase random solid solution.
The target specimen has approximately 1 wt.% oxygen contamination.
The model is applicable from 40 to 1200 K.
Lattice and electronic thermal-conductivity contributions are nearly equal below 200 K.
From 300 to 1200 K, the model predicts lattice conductivity approximately 20–25% below conventional Debye predictions.
SPS-induced grain structure and residual stress alter effective elastic constants and phonon propagation in HfNbTaTiZr.
DFT-derived elastic constants yield more accurate phonon group velocities and lifetimes than simplified Debye assumptions.
A separate electronic-transport parametrization based on measured carrier densities keeps electronic and lattice contributions decoupled.
The predicted electronic contribution will follow metallic Drude behavior.
Traditional Debye-temperature models conflate lattice and electronic conduction.
The model's predictive applicability is limited to SPS-produced alloys containing less than 1 wt.% oxygen.
Prediction accuracy is sensitive to uncertainty in DFT-derived elastic constants and to unmodeled microstructural defects.
A lattice-conductivity deviation greater than 10%, or failure to observe the stated temperature-dependent channel separation, would falsify the hypothesis.
